observations.text: The full saved desktop course has a stable centered reading column, a distinct heading and breadcrumb, separated paragraphs, three clear section rules, and a visible final note. No gross text overlap, horizontal clipping, missing section, or blank figure is visible at the supplied whole-image scale.

The saved viewport shows N59's opening heading, charge and particle definitions, and the introductory Figure 103 context. Prose and bold terms are readable, line spacing is clear, and text stays within the column. The inherited polarization-viewport filename is not taken as evidence of a polarization section.

Figure 103 is nonblank and fully contained in its saved frame. Both circular outlines, the central filled nucleus with a plus sign, and the outlined electron markers with minus signs are visible and separated; no label or outline is clipped by the frame. The bound DOM media width is the unchanged 640 px contract.

The complete mobile course forms one consistent narrow column from the wrapped heading through the final note. Paragraphs, three section rules, the figure, and its caption remain distinct with no visible horizontal spill, overlap, missing block, or bottom-content truncation at whole-image scale.

At the saved 390x844 viewport, the title and breadcrumb wrap within the available width, and opening definitions and bold terms remain readable without collisions. The next paragraph meets the lower screenshot edge as ordinary viewport continuation; the whole image shows its continuation, not layout clipping.

The mobile Figure 103 frame is nonblank and preserves the same visible composition as desktop. Circular outlines, nucleus, plus sign, electron markers, and minus signs remain contained and discernible without collision or edge clipping. The bound DOM media width is the unchanged 358 px contract.

Both whole views place the centered Figure 103 caption directly beneath the atom diagram with clear separation from the following prose. The preceding visible text calls it an old simplified atom picture and distinguishes its circular lines from measured electron paths and real size scale. Caption, diagram, and nearby text therefore match in display context; this is not a new scientific or source-fidelity approval.
